The matter action authorization check `if (!isAdmin && !isAssigned && role !== "client")` never throws for client-role users, so an authenticated client can POST to /matters/:id with any matterId and run transition_status (prisma.matter.update at line 211), create_note, create_message, upload_document, send_status_notice, or export_binder on matters they do not own — nothing binds the attacker-selected matter to the client's own client record, unlike the loader (line 75).

update_task_status takes taskId from the request and calls prisma.task.update({ where: { id: taskId } }) without verifying the task belongs to the currently authorized matter, allowing a staff user assigned to one matter to change status/completion of tasks in other matters.

approve_message takes messageId from the request and calls prisma.message.update without binding it to the authorized matterId, so a staff user can approve draft messages belonging to other matters they cannot access.
